Projects

FIRST Robotics Competition — Team 3875 Red Storm Robotics

As Design Lead for FRC Team 3875, I led the full mechanical design of a ball-intake-and-shooting robot across three iterations — Alpha, Beta, and Charlie — improving average match score from 57 to 126 balls per match.

Iteration 1
Alpha — Proof of Concept

BlockCAD prototype to plan mechanism placement and electrical routing. No manufacturing — purely a spatial planning exercise.

Iteration 2
Beta — First Built Robot

4-bar intake with a single Kraken X60 motor at 2:1 reduction. Brush-based carousel indexer. Single stationary shooter. Averaged 57 balls/match across two competitions.

Iteration 3
Charlie — States Redesign

Dual-roller intake, cone-shaped PETG indexer with grip tape, 3-stage hooded shooter with custom gears and sheet-metal flywheels. Averaged 126 balls/match at states.

Subsystem deep-dive
Carousel Indexer

Redesigned from a brush-based middle piece to a PETG cone with grip tape. The cone geometry funnels balls down and prevents back-spin, increasing indexing throughput by 150%.

OnshapePETG 3D PrintGrip Tape
3-Stage Hooded Shooter

Redesigned from a stationary single-stage shooter to a 3-stage system with an adjustable hood. Custom-designed gears control hood angle. Sheet-metal flywheels conserve rotational momentum for consistent shot accuracy. Dual Kraken X60 motors at 1:1 ratio.

Custom GearsSheet MetalFlywheelsFusion 360
Chassis & Electrical Integration

Designed the chassis layout to integrate all electrical components — motor controllers, PDH, radio, and gyro — coordinating with the electrical lead to ensure proper routing and accessibility.

OnshapeElectrical LayoutCNC Machined Parts
4-Bar Intake System

Evolved from a single-roller 4-bar linkage to a dual-roller system with reduced ball compression. The 4-bar geometry provides collision resilience and consistent ground contact. Intake speed improved 40% from Beta.
